verification: ladder reference (reference/problem-ladder.md, archetype #2) states shapes.png has 6 known shapes

independent cv2 recount this session: GaussianBlur -> THRESH_BINARY_INV|OTSU -> MORPH_CLOSE -> findContours(RETR_EXTERNAL) -> area filter at 0.1% of frame -> 6 contours survive, vertex counts [4,4,8,4,3,8] (quad, quad, ~circle, quad, triangle, ~circle)

caption_reference_outputs.model: Salesforce/blip-image-captioning-base, BlipForConditionalGeneration, CPU, run in this session against sample_14.png
caption_reference_outputs.unconditioned: a white background with a colorful geometric pattern
caption_reference_outputs.\"a photo of\": a photo of a group of different shapes
caption_reference_outputs.note: either of these (or anything in the same spirit -- mentions shapes/geometric figures on a plain background) is a fine caption; exact wording is never graded

the_planted_trap_verified.prompt: "there are a total of" fed as the conditional text prefix to the same BLIP checkpoint
the_planted_trap_verified.output: "there are a total of 10 different shapes"

also_tried.\"how many shapes are in this image?\": echoes the question back verbatim, no answer -- this checkpoint is captioning-only, not VQA-tuned
also_tried.\"the number of shapes in this image is\: "...a square, triangle, and circle" -- doesn't even produce a number, lists shape names incoherently

the_planted_trap_verified.lesson: every way of coaxing a direct count out of this model either refuses, rambles, or states a specific wrong number with full confidence. There is no prompt variant that reliably gets the right number from the captioning model alone.

scoring.full_marks: shape_count is exactly 6, arrived at by some check independent of the model's free-text output (cv2 contour count, manual count against the image, template matching, anything deterministic/verifiable), AND caption is a plausible one-line description of the image (does not need to match the reference wording).
scoring.bonus: Explicitly runs or mentions a captioning/VQA model, notices it gives an unreliable or wrong count when pushed, and says so -- naming the specific failure mode (not just 'VLMs can be wrong' in the abstract) is the strongest possible answer here and mirrors the ladder's own stated line for this archetype.
scoring.the_trap_landing: shape_count is reported as 10 (or any other number that traces back to an unverified model utterance) with no independent check -- this is the exact, reproduced failure this fixture was built to catch.
scoring.no_credit: shape_count is correct (6) but arrived at with no stated method and no artifact showing how -- unverifiable is not the same as wrong, but it isn't full marks either per the project's standing evaluation rubric (processes, not just final numbers, are what's being scored).
scoring.caption_scoring: almost impossible to get wrong here since nothing is graded on exact wording -- the only miss is skipping it entirely or hand-typing a caption with no model run at all, when the brief specifically asked for a generated description.

forks_left_open_in_the_brief.fork: How to produce either number -- model, cv2, eyeballing -- is left unstated.
forks_left_open_in_the_brief.correct: Any method is fine for the caption; only a verifiable method is fine for the count, because the count is the one the brief implicitly promises to be exact ('an exact count').
forks_left_open_in_the_brief.scoring: see full_marks / the_trap_landing above -- the fork isn't really 'which answer is right', it's 'which process produces a number you can stand behind.'

traps_planted: The word 'exact' in the brief ('an exact count') is itself a hint that free-association from a captioning model is not going to satisfy the ask -- a candidate who reads past it and takes the model's number at face value has missed something stated in plain English, not just a hidden gotcha.

The cached BLIP checkpoint is captioning-only; treating it as if it understands questions (feeding it 'how many...?' and expecting an answer) silently fails (echoes the prompt) rather than erroring, which looks like a working-but-useless result if not checked against anything.
what_a_strong_answer_looks_like: Generates the caption with an actual model call, not a hand-written guess.
Counts shapes with a deterministic pass (contours, template matching, or careful visual inspection against the overlay) rather than trusting any model's stated number.
If it tried asking the model for a count first, reports what it got and explains why it didn't trust it.
Writes output/description.json with a count of 6.
verification_available_to_the_candidate: Open the image directly -- six distinct, non-overlapping shapes on a plain background, easy to recount by eye in a few seconds. The honest check is cheap here, which is exactly why skipping it (and shipping whatever the model said) is the failure being probed for.
